clue.text: Family money upfront needed for suede leather?

indicators.note: upfront says the money piece comes at the front, before the family piece

parts.note: bucks is slang for dollars, money
kin are one's family, relatives

explanation.surface: A family needs cash in advance to buy some suede.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckskin is soft leather made from deer hide, often with a suede-like finish.

clue.text: Hound, British, something worth having

parts.note: an asset is a valuable thing to own

explanation.surface: A British dog is described as a real prize.
explanation.definitionFit: A basset is a short-legged breed of hunting dog, a type of hound.

clue.text: Unfinished survey material

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter of the survey word is cut off

parts.note: to canvass is to survey opinion, as pollsters do

explanation.surface: A half-done survey of some fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Canvas is a heavy woven cloth used for sails, tents and paintings.

clue.text: Flat in raised area in Herts town

indicators.note: in places the flat word inside the raised-area word

parts.note: a stage is a raised platform for performers
flat means level or even

explanation.surface: A level patch on a raised platform in a Hertfordshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Herts is the usual short form of Hertfordshire, an English county just north of London; Stevenage is a new town there.
explanation.definitionFit: Stevenage is a town in Hertfordshire, England, the county shortened to Herts.

clue.text: Daring sideline that's criminal?

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters of the two words are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A risky little side business that breaks the law.
explanation.definitionFit: Trading shares on confidential information is an illegal, risky sideline for those with privileged knowledge.

clue.text: Fit of shivering after spin in city

indicators.note: after places the shivering piece after the spin piece

parts.note: PR (public relations) is spin, the art of putting a slant on news
an ague is a fever with shivering fits

explanation.surface: Someone shivers feverishly after a dizzy spin around a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Prague is the capital city of the Czech Republic.

clue.text: Unusual graduate makes one dance?

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or unusual
BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: An odd graduate is moved to dance.
explanation.walkthrough: RUM as an adjective means strange, an old-fashioned British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance.

clue.text: Importance of a vast rig at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: An oil rig at sea matters a lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravitas is seriousness or weightiness, the quality that gives a person importance.

clue.text: Confuse adjacent angles? Not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely says only part of the phrase is used, a run of letters inside it

explanation.surface: A geometry student muddles neighbouring angles.
explanation.definitionFit: To entangle is to tangle up or confuse, as in a muddled situation.

clue.text: Inept artisan engaged by college man — he causes delay

indicators.note: engaged by means held inside, so the shuffled letters go within the college official

parts.note: a proctor is a university official who keeps discipline

indicators.note: inept means clumsy, so the craftsman word is reshaped

explanation.surface: A clumsy craftsman is hired by a university official who keeps putting things off.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who habitually postpones tasks is a delayer by nature.

clue.text: Gloomy as newspaper's been taken?

parts.note: the Sun is a British tabloid newspaper; the 's is short for has
less suggests something taken away, as in sums: six less two

explanation.surface: Someone is downcast because their newspaper has been stolen.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid paper: if the Sun has been taken, the result is the Sun less.
explanation.definitionFit: Without sunlight a place is dark and dismal, so lacking sun suits gloomy.

clue.text: Unrestrained bombast about a politician

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the speech goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a rant is a loud bombastic speech
MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician

explanation.surface: A politician speaks with unrestrained bluster.
explanation.definitionFit: Rampant means spreading without control, unchecked, unrestrained.

clue.text: Remove article in Celtic language

indicators.note: in places the article inside the language

parts.note: Erse is an old name for Scottish or Irish Gaelic
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Delete an article written in Gaelic.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase is to rub out or delete, removing something written.

clue.text: I'm obliged to probe way of expressing commands

indicators.note: to probe means to go into, so the thanks goes inside the word for style of speech

parts.note: diction is a style of speaking or choice of words
ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: Someone grateful wants to investigate how orders are phrased.
explanation.definitionFit: Dictation can mean the giving of orders, authoritative commands from above.

clue.text: Lawn had rails adapted to provide barrier

indicators.note: adapted means changed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A garden's grass and railings are converted into a fence.
explanation.walkthrough: The Roman wall ran across northern England to keep out northern tribes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman fortification across northern Britain was built as a defensive barrier.

clue.text: Improving appearance at floor level?

parts.note: looks like a description of a home makeover, but means polishing what is on your feet

explanation.definitionFit: Polishing footwear smartens the look of what is worn nearest the ground.

clue.text: Attempt at goal from half-way line? It has little chance of success

definitions.text: Attempt at goal from half-way line?
definitions.meaning: a shot taken from a great distance, as in football

definitions.text: It has little chance of success
definitions.meaning: an outsider or unlikely venture, a bet at big odds

explanation.definitionFit: A distant strike at goal and an unlikely bet both describe a low-probability attempt.

clue.text: Tradesman making rude remark about source of supply

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the mocking word goes round the source

parts.note: a jeer is a mocking, rude remark
a well is a source of water or oil

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper makes an insulting comment about where his stock comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: A dealer in gems and watches is a tradesman of a particular kind.

clue.text: Making too much effort, wander beginning to end, tire oxen out

indicators.note: the first letter of the wander word is shifted to the end

parts.note: to rove is to wander

indicators.note: out means disordered, so these letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A farmer straining to plough wanders from start to finish and wears out the oxen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to end' moves R from the front of ROVE to give OVER; 'out' turns TIRE OXEN into EXERTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Too much strain or exertion is the state of pushing oneself beyond what is wise.

clue.text: Wrongful intention guy includes in charge

indicators.note: includes means the man word holds the abbreviation inside it

parts.note: a guy is a man, a male

explanation.surface: A man in authority has sinister motives.
explanation.definitionFit: Malice is the wish to do harm, an evil intent behind an act.

clue.text: Race in sea going over line

indicators.note: going over means placed above, first in this down entry

parts.note: the Med is short for the Mediterranean Sea
a ley is a ley line, an alignment of ancient sites

explanation.surface: A competitor in the sea passes over the finishing line.
explanation.definitionFit: A medley is a swimming race in which several strokes are used in turn.

clue.text: Girl having information about work, getting state payment (new)

indicators.note: about means the information word goes round the work symbol

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
W is the symbol for work in physics
the dole is British slang for unemployment benefit

explanation.surface: A young woman with details about a job is claiming benefit, it says.
explanation.definitionFit: Gwendolen is a female first name, as in Wilde's comedy, so it fits a girl.

clue.text: Senior member to provide foreign currency

parts.note: to do can mean to provide, as in a pub that does food
the yen is the currency of Japan

explanation.surface: An elder statesman is asked to supply some foreign money.
explanation.definitionFit: A doyen is the most respected or longest-serving person in a group.

clue.text: Room — special one

parts.note: an ace counts as one in cards

explanation.surface: A room described as one of a kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Room in the sense of free area or capacity is a synonym of extent and expanse.

clue.text: Not quite half century that's happy and peaceful

indicators.note: not quite means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: the word half itself, cut short
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a century
yon is an old word for that; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: Almost fifty years old, someone is content and calm.
explanation.definitionFit: Halcyon days are idyllic, a time of calm contentment and peace.

clue.text: Quartet in experiment of little importance

indicators.note: in puts the numeral inside the test word

parts.note: a trial is a test or experiment
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A test involving a group of four turns out to be insignificant.
explanation.definitionFit: Trivial means trifling or petty, not mattering much.

clue.text: Seat a lot of people, getting energy in the end

indicators.note: the final letter is replaced by E, the symbol for energy

parts.note: a throng is a large crowd

explanation.surface: A large crowd finally gets lively and someone takes a seat.
explanation.definitionFit: A throne is a monarch's ceremonial chair, a seat of state.

clue.text: What might be represented as ne'er grey?

definitions.text: What might be represented as ne'er grey?

indicators.note: represented means presented again in another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A riddle asking what is never grey.
explanation.definitionFit: Lush foliage is green, never grey, so the plant growth fits the riddle.
